title: A nightly computer-use agent turns recent commits into QA evidence
friendlyTitle: An AI agent can test yesterday’s software changes overnight
summary: A SaaS engineer describes a computer-use QA agent that reviews recent commits, tests user-facing flows, records screenshots and reproduction steps, and files detailed issues. The setup combines user-level access with read-only code context and scheduled execution.
friendlySummary: One engineer uses an agent to read recent code changes, try the product like a user, take screenshots, and report bugs. The agent runs on a schedule and keeps notes for its next test.
whyItMatters: This is a reusable pattern for supervised automation: give an agent realistic user interfaces, enough technical context to investigate failures, and a structured place to report evidence. It can reduce repetitive manual testing without giving the agent authority to silently ship fixes.
friendlyWhyItMatters: This can save testing time while still leaving people in charge of reviewing and fixing important problems.
